questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct direct form of the sentence.

She said, since it was evening, she had to go for a run.

options.text: She said, “It is evening I must ran.”
She said, “It is evening I might go for a run.”
She said, “It is evening I should go for a run.”
She said, “It is evening I must go for a run.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"she had to go for a run"** indicates obligation.
 
• It is usually conveyed by the modal verb **"must"** in direct speech.
 
• So, in **direct speech**, it changes to "I must go for a run."

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: *''She said, “It is evening I must go for a run.”*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because the past simple "ran" is not used with "must" - we use the base form of the verb, which is "run."
 
• **Option 2 **uses "might," which indicates possibility rather than obligation. Therefore, it is not a suitable choice here.
 
• **Option 3** uses "should," which indicates advice or suggestion. Although "should" might sometimes be used to indicate a kind of obligation, in this context "must" is a better fit because it more accurately reflects the speaker's sense of duty or obligation to go for a run.

questions.question:
The given sentence is in active voice. Change the voice of the sentence. Select the correct option from the sentences given in options.

Vasant has delivered the speech.

options.text: Vasant delivers the speech on time.
The speech was delivered by Vasant.
The speech was timely delivered by Vasant.
The speech has been delivered by Vasant.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the **active voice,** the subject of the sentence (Vasant) performs the action (delivered the speech).
 
• In the **passive voice,** the object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• The action (has delivered the speech) is done by the subject, which is now **"the speech".**
 
• The original subject (Vasant) becomes part of a prepositional phrase (by Vasant) showing who performed the action.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is:* 'The speech has been delivered by Vasant.'*

questions.question:
Some parts of a few sentences have been jumbled up, and labelled A, B, C and D. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

My years in my father’s house

A. would have been unbearable had

B. the feel of his hand clutching mine, his

C. I not had my brother. I never forgot

D. refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct sequence** of these sentences is **ACBD**. Here's why:
 
• "My years in my father’s house" is the main clause, which can stand by itself as a complete sentence.
 
• **"A. **would have been unbearable had" is the start of the next part of the sentence.
 
 
• **It provides a continuation** to the main clause, implying that something made the years bearable.
 
 
 
• **"C. **I not had my brother." This sentence fits well with the previous part (A) as it provides the answer to what made the years bearable - having a brother.
 
 
• **It forms a complete and meaningful sentence** when put after A, "My years in my father’s house would have been unbearable had I not had my brother."
 
• "I never forgot" is the continuation of the first part of the sentence, focusing on the protagonist's memories related to his brother.
 
 
 
• **"B. **the feel of his hand clutching mine, his" This sentence logically follows the previous part (C) as it provides more specific memories of his brother.
 
• **"D. **refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise."
 
 
• This **sentence fits well **at the end as it rounds off the sentiment of the previous parts and completes the overall thought.
 
 

Therefore, the** complete sentence** is: *"My years in my father’s house would have been unbearable had I not had my brother. I never forgot the feel of his hand clutching mine, his refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise." Hence, the correct sequence is ACBD.*

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

That will truly / been a milestone to / celebrate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'been a milestone to'.**

• The part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error is:** "been a milestone to".**
 
• This **error is related to** tense consistency. 
 
• Tenses should not be mixed within a sentence unless there is a shift in the time frame within the context of the sentence.
 
• In this case, the **correct tense should be** future, so** 'been' **should be replaced with** 'be'.**
 
• **'Been' **is a past participle and doesn't fit here as the rest of the sentence is in future tense indicated by **'will'.**

So the **correct sentence **should be:* "That will truly be a milestone to celebrate."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3 is **"toppled".**
 
• **In the context of the sentence**, the man with the shotgun is being aggressive towards the guard, hence "toppled" makes sense because it suggests he forcefully knocked or pushed the guard onto the floor, especially given that this action followed a kick between the shoulder blades.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'The man with the shotgun pushed the guard to his knees. He handed up the shotgun to his partner and yanked the guard's wrists up behind his back and locked them together with a pair of handcuffs. He **toppled **him onto the floor with a kick between the shoulder blades. Then he took his shotgun back and (4) ______ to the security gate at the end of the counter. He was short and heavy and moved with peculiar slowness. “Buzz him (5) ______,” his partner said.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are less suitable:
 
 
• **"Ascended"** means to rise or go up, which doesn't fit the context because the guard is being brought down, not lifted up.
 
• **"Placed" **is too gentle a word to describe the aggressive actions taking place.
 
• "**Straightened" **would imply the guard was being put upright or in a correct position, which again contradicts the aggressive context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'** i.e. **'Went over'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4 is **"went over".**
 
• **In the given context, **the man with the shotgun is moving towards the security gate at the end of the counter.
 
• The phrase** "went over"** is used to mean 'moved towards' or 'proceeded to' in this case.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'The man with the shotgun pushed the guard to his knees. He handed up the shotgun to his partner and yanked the guard's wrists up behind his back and locked them together with a pair of handcuffs. He toppled him onto the floor with a kick between the shoulder blades. Then he took his shotgun back and** went over** to the security gate at the end of the counter. He was short and heavy and moved with peculiar slowness. “Buzz him (5) ______,” his partner said.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are less suitable:
 
 
• **"Went under" **usually means to go beneath something or to fail, neither of which fits the context.
 
• **"Went along"** would imply the man is going with someone or agreeing with them, which doesn't make sense here.
 
• **"Went besides"** is not grammatically correct; the proper phrase is "went beside" which means to go next to something or someone, but this does not fit the context as well as "went over".

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4' **i.e.** 'In'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5 is **"in".**
 
• In this context,** "Buzz him in"** means to use an intercom or other electronic device to allow the person (in this case, the man with the shotgun) access to a restricted area.
 
• **"Buzz"** refers to the sound that these devices often make, and **"in"** indicates the granting of access or entry.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'The man with the shotgun pushed the guard to his knees. He handed up the shotgun to his partner and yanked the guard's wrists up behind his back and locked them together with a pair of handcuffs. He toppled him onto the floor with a kick between the shoulder blades. Then he took his shotgun back and went over to the security gate at the end of the counter. He was short and heavy and moved with peculiar slowness. “Buzz him** in,**” his partner said.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Here's why the other options don't fit as well:
 
 
• **"Buzz him to" **isn't a common or correct phrase. It would imply the man is being "buzzed" to a specific location, which doesn't make sense in this scenario.
 
• **"Buzz him on" **could suggest the man is being encouraged or cheered on, which also doesn't fit the context.
 
• **"Buzz him with"** would imply the man is being "buzzed" using a specific tool or method, but the sentence doesn't provide any additional information that would justify the use of "with".
